rules.text: Flag handwritten markings (e.g., price, date) on packaging as anomalies, even if the package structure is intact.
rules.justification: The agent missed the anomaly in D2_0170 because it focused on structural defects. The actual anomaly is a handwritten price/date mark, which is a contamination/defect in retail QC but was ignored.

rules.text: Do not flag minor wrinkles, creases, or scuffs on flexible packaging edges as defects if they are consistent with normal handling.
rules.justification: All three FP items were flagged for minor surface imperfections (wrinkles, creases) on flexible bags. These are common artifacts of handling and storage, not manufacturing defects.

rules.text: Flag any large, irregular hole or missing material on the top flap or edges of the box as a physical defect.
rules.justification: The agent missed a clear structural failure (a large hole) on the top flap. This is a definitive physical defect distinct from minor wear or printing errors.

rules.text: Do not flag specular glare or bright white reflections on glossy packaging surfaces as defects.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly identified a light reflection on the glossy box surface as an anomaly. Glare is a common optical artifact in retail photography, not a product defect.

rules.text: Do not flag standard packaging geometry or slight edge curvature as crushing or deformation.
rules.justification: The agent over-flagged items as 'crushed' or 'deformed' likely due to perspective distortion or the natural shape of the packaging, rather than actual structural damage.

rules.text: Flag cartons with attached plastic straw wrappers or straws as anomalies, even if the label print is perfect.
rules.justification: The agent missed anomalies where a straw or wrapper was physically attached to the carton. These are distinct physical defects not present in reference images, regardless of label quality.

rules.text: Do not flag minor label smudges or print imperfections if the overall packaging design and text layout match the reference.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly flagged a normal item due to a minor smudge. If the design matches the reference, minor print artifacts should be tolerated as normal variation.

rules.text: Do not flag items as anomalies solely based on different packaging designs if the product type and brand are consistent with the reference set.
rules.justification: The agent flagged a normal item because the design differed from the reference. Different designs within the same product category are normal variations, not defects.

rules.text: Flag packs with open top flaps or torn cardboard as anomalies, even if the printed face is intact.
rules.justification: The agent missed physical damage (open flap, torn cardboard) because it focused on the printed face or orientation. Structural integrity is a valid defect.

rules.text: Flag packs with completely different color schemes or graphics as anomalies, overriding 'design variation' logic.
rules.justification: The agent hesitated on a pack with a yellow diagonal stripe vs red reference. Drastic visual mismatches in color/graphic are anomalies, not variations.

rules.text: Flag bottles with missing labels or exposed dark liquid as anomalies, even if the bottle shape is intact.
rules.justification: The agent failed to recognize that the absence of a label and the visibility of dark liquid are definitive signs of a packaging defect or wrong fill, distinct from normal product variations.

rules.text: Do not flag bottles with intact caps and labels as anomalies solely due to slight rotation or perceived misalignment.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly identified a normal bottle as defective because the label appeared rotated. This is a common artifact of product placement on shelves and should be tolerated.

rules.text: Flag small, high-contrast white spots on dark or purple packaging as defects, even if they appear as minor surface marks.
rules.justification: The agent missed a small white mark on the purple cup because it was subtle. On dark backgrounds, even tiny white spots are likely defects (scratches or residue) and should be flagged.

rules.text: Do not flag crinkled or uneven foil seals on the rim of cup noodles as defects if the seal remains intact.
rules.justification: The agent flagged a 'tear' on the lid, but the reference showed similar crinkling. Foil seals on these products often have natural manufacturing wrinkles that are not defects.
